cls: Thrombopoietin receptor agonist (peptibody) - haematopoietic growth factor
pharm: A thrombopoietin-receptor agonist (peptibody) that stimulates platelet production, used for chronic immune thrombocytopenia
quick: Initial 1 mcg/kg SC once weekly, titrate by 1 mcg/kg to platelets >=50 x10^9/L (max 10 mcg/kg/week)
Use only if benefit outweighs risk; crosses placenta, may affect fetal platelets
Caution; unknown if excreted in milk
No specific dose adjustment; limited data in impairment
Use with caution; thrombotic risk with portal hypertension
Weekly CBC/platelets until stable then monthly; blood film for morphology
summary: Romiplostim is a thrombopoietin-receptor agonist (a Fc-peptide fusion 'peptibody') that binds and activates the thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor (c-Mpl) on megakaryocytes, increasing platelet production. It is indicated for thrombocytopenia in adults and children with chronic immune (idiopathic) thrombocytopenia who have had an insufficient response to corticosteroids, immunoglobulins or splenectomy, and (in adults) for thrombocytopenia of certain settings such as haematopoietic syndrome of acute radiation. It is given as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection, started at 1 mcg/kg and titrated in 1 mcg/kg steps (maximum 10 mcg/kg/week) to maintain a platelet count of at least 50 x10^9/L while avoiding excessive counts. Treatment must not be used to normalise platelet counts. Key risks include thrombosis/thromboembolism (increased with excessive platelet rise), worsening thrombocytopenia and bleeding after discontinuation, and reticulin deposition in the bone marrow. Platelet counts require close weekly monitoring during titration.
indications: Chronic immune (idiopathic) thrombocytopenia (ITP) in adults with insufficient response to corticosteroids, immunoglobulins or splenectomy
Chronic ITP in paediatric patients (1 year and older) for at least 6 months with insufficient response to corticosteroids, immunoglobulins or splenectomy
Acute radiation syndrome - haematopoietic subsyndrome (adult and paediatric) to increase survival following exposure to myelosuppressive radiation doses

dosage.n: Recalculate dose for weight changes (use actual body weight)

Discontinue if platelet count does not increase sufficiently after 4 weeks at the maximum 10 mcg/kg/week

admin: Administer subcutaneously once weekly; calculate dose using actual body weight
Obtain a CBC including platelet count weekly until a stable dose maintaining platelets >=50 x10^9/L for at least 4 weeks, then monthly
Do not use to normalise platelet counts; reduce the dose if platelets exceed about 200-400 x10^9/L per label thresholds
After discontinuation, monitor platelet counts weekly for at least 2 weeks because thrombocytopenia may worsen below baseline with increased bleeding risk
Consider a peripheral blood smear to monitor for new morphologic abnormalities (reticulin/marrow changes)
moa: Romiplostim is an Fc-peptide fusion protein (peptibody) that contains peptide domains binding to and activating the thrombopoietin receptor (c-Mpl) on megakaryocyte progenitors. It mimics the action of endogenous thrombopoietin by stimulating the proliferation and differentiation of megakaryocytes and increasing platelet production, though it shares no amino-acid sequence homology with endogenous TPO (reducing cross-reactive antibody risk). The result is a dose-dependent increase in circulating platelets that begins within days of dosing.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to romiplostim or any component
relative: Chronic liver disease/portal hypertension (thrombotic risk including portal vein thrombosis)
Pre-existing bone-marrow disorders (e.g. myelodysplastic syndrome - risk of disease progression/blast increase)
monitor: Platelet count and CBC (weekly during titration, then monthly)
Bleeding, especially after dose reduction or discontinuation
Peripheral blood smear for morphologic changes (marrow reticulin)

preg: There are limited data on romiplostim in pregnancy; it crosses the placenta and may affect fetal platelet counts. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; a pregnancy surveillance programme exists for some products.
lact: It is not known whether romiplostim is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects in the infant, a decision should be made to discontinue breastfeeding or the drug, weighing the importance of treatment to the mother.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is recommended; experience in patients with renal impairment is limited, so use with caution and standard platelet-guided titration.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment. In chronic liver disease, thrombopoietin-receptor agonists carry a risk of thrombotic events, including portal vein thrombosis, particularly if platelet counts rise excessively.

moderate: Anticoagulant and antiplatelet drugs - bleeding/thrombosis balance is altered as platelet counts change; monitor closely
Other agents affecting platelet counts - additive or counteracting effects on platelets
interactions.diagnostics: Raises platelet counts; monitor CBC and peripheral smear; interpret platelet trends in relation to dosing

common: Upper respiratory tract infection, abdominal pain (in children)
serious: Thrombotic/thromboembolic events (DVT, PE, MI, stroke, portal vein thrombosis)
Worsening thrombocytopenia and bleeding after discontinuation
Progression of myelodysplastic syndrome (increased blasts) in MDS patients
Loss of response (consider neutralising antibodies or marrow changes)
emergency: Acute thrombosis (chest pain, breathlessness, limb swelling, stroke symptoms)

monitoring: CBC with platelet count weekly during dose titration, then monthly once stable
Platelet counts weekly for at least 2 weeks after discontinuation (risk of worsening thrombocytopenia)
Peripheral blood smear for new red/white-cell morphologic abnormalities (marrow reticulin)
counsel: This weekly injection raises your platelet count to reduce bleeding from low platelets
The aim is a safe platelet level, not a normal one, so the dose is adjusted by regular blood tests - keep your appointments
Report signs of a clot: chest pain, breathlessness, leg swelling/pain, or sudden weakness, numbness or speech problems
If treatment is stopped, your platelets may drop below where they started and bleeding can increase - attend follow-up blood tests
Report unusual bruising, bleeding or persistent headaches
pk: Platelet count begins to rise within several days; peak platelet response typically around days 12-16 after a dose
Serum concentrations vary and correlate poorly with platelet response; effect is platelet-count driven
Serum half-life approximately 1-34 days (median around 3.5 days), influenced by platelet TPO-receptor mass
Weekly dosing maintains platelet response; effect wanes over 1-2 weeks after stopping
Store refrigerated (2-8 C), protect from light; do not freeze; reconstituted solution per label
pearls: Titrate by platelet count (target >=50 x10^9/L), NOT to normalise counts - excessive platelet rise increases thrombosis risk
Discontinue if no adequate response after 4 weeks at the maximum 10 mcg/kg/week
After stopping, thrombocytopenia can worsen below baseline with increased bleeding - monitor platelets for at least 2 weeks
Risks include thrombosis (including portal vein thrombosis in liver disease), marrow reticulin formation, and MDS progression
It is a peptibody with no sequence homology to endogenous TPO, reducing cross-reactive antibody risk
Also approved for the haematopoietic subsyndrome of acute radiation syndrome as a single 10 mcg/kg dose
missed: Romiplostim is usually given weekly by a healthcare professional. If a weekly dose is missed, contact your provider to reschedule; the dose may be given when feasible and platelet counts will guide further dosing. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose may cause an excessive increase in platelet count and an associated risk of thrombotic/thromboembolic complications. There is no specific antidote. Discontinue romiplostim, monitor platelet counts closely, and manage thrombotic events as clinically indicated; restart at a lower dose once platelets fall to an appropriate range.
